MZEN was introduced to address the failure of classical Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and standard pose-free NeRFs in industrial imaging contexts where optical zoom changes significantly [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that MZEN is designed for industrial imaging systems (microscopes, inspection cameras, SEMs) where classical Structure-from-Motion (SfM) fails due to mechanical zoom mechanisms and micron-scale stage movements. It further explains that standard pose-free NeRFs fail in these contexts because they assume fixed or small zoom perturbations, which breaks down when magnification changes significantly, leading to unidentifiable coupling of translation, scale, and focal length. MZEN addresses this by modeling optical zoom as a learnable intrinsic parameter and using cross-zoom pose registration.
